property_summary: After a call to Collect(0.5 ether) by an account with 1 ether balance and unlock time met, the reference contract's Acc balance getter returns 0.5 ether while the buggy contract returns 0.75 ether due to halving the Put amount.

After an account Puts 2 ether then Collects 1 ether (MinSum=1 ether, unlock time met), the reference contract returns Acc balance = 1 ether, but the buggy contract (halving Put) returns Acc balance = 2 ether because only half the Put amount was added.

After Alice Puts 2 ether with block.timestamp unlock time and warps forward to meet it, then Collects 1 ether, the reference contract's Acc balance for Alice becomes 1 ether, while the buggy contract (halving Put) becomes 1.5 ether.

After Alice Puts 2 ether (unlock time now), then Bob Puts 2 ether (unlock time now), warps forward, Alice Collects 1 ether. In the reference, Alice's remaining balance is 1 ether; in the buggy version (Put halves), Alice's balance is 1.5 ether.

Alice deposits 2 ether via Put (time zero), warps past unlock, then Collects 0.5 ether; the reference Acc balance for Alice returns 1.5 ether (2 - 0.5), while the buggy version returns 1.75 ether (1 - 0.5) due to halving the Put amount.
After putting 1 ether at timestamp 10, Collect(1 ether) at timestamp 10 succeeds in the bug (≥) but fails in the reference (>), so c.Collect returns successfully in M but reverts in P.

After putting 1 ether at timestamp 10, Collect(1 ether) at timestamp 10 succeeds in the bug (due to >=) but fails in the reference (due to >), so the reference reverts while the buggy version does not.

After putting 1 ether at timestamp 10, Collect(1 ether) at timestamp 10 succeeds in the bug (due to >=) but fails in the reference (due to >), so the reference reverts while the buggy version does not.

After putting 1 ether at timestamp 10, Collect(1 ether) at timestamp 10 succeeds in the bug (due to >=) but fails in the reference (due to >), so the reference reverts while the buggy version does not.

After Put sends 1 ether at timestamp 10, then at timestamp 10 Collect(1 ether) succeeds in the buggy contract due to >= but reverts in the reference due to >; the buggy version's Collect returns successfully (no revert) while the reference reverts, causing c.Collect to behave differently.

After funding an account with 2 ether and calling Collect(0.5 ether) when unlockTime is satisfied, the reference C reduces balance by 0.5 ether resulting in 1.5 ether, while the buggy M sets balance to 0. The state variable Acc(bob).balance diverges.

After funding an account with 2 ether, setting unlockTime in the past, and calling Collect(0.5 ether), the reference contract reduces balance by 0.5 ether while the buggy contract sets balance to 0; reading Acc(bob).balance diverges.

After funding bob with exactly MinSum (1 ether) and setting unlockTime to a past timestamp, calling Collect(1 ether) causes the reference contract to set bob's balance to 0 (deducting 1 ether from 1 ether leaves 0) while the buggy contract also sets balance to 0; both succeed, but the reference allows the Collect call while the buggy one also allows it, so there is no divergence in this case. Actually choosing Collect(_am) with _am > 0 and exactly equal to current balance will not show divergence because both end up at 0. To get divergence, we need Collect to succeed (condition satisfied) and reference leaves non-zero balance while bug leaves 0. So we set bob's balance to 2 ether, then call Collect(1 ether): reference balance becomes 1 ether, buggy balance becomes 0 ether. Divergence at Acc(bob).balance.

Bob deposits 2 ether, then calls Collect(0.5 ether) with unlockTime in the past; reference contract reduces balance to 1.5 ether, buggy contract sets balance to 0, causing Acc(bob).balance to diverge.

Bob deposits 2 ether, then calls Collect(0.5 ether) with unlockTime in the past; the reference C reduces balance to 1.5 ether, while the buggy M sets balance to 0, causing Acc(bob).balance to diverge.

After a user deposits 2 ether and calls Collect(2 ether) when MinSum is 0.5 ether and unlockTime has passed, the reference contract sends 2 ether and decreases balance to 0, while the buggy contract allows Collect to succeed even when balance is insufficient (but balance becomes -1 ether due to underflow, causing the returned balance to be a huge number). The concrete divergence is that c.Acc(user).balance differs: reference returns 0, buggy returns 2^256 - 1.

After user deposits 1 ether and calls Collect(2 ether) when MinSum is 0.5 ether and unlockTime passed, reference reverts due to insufficient balance, but buggy succeeds and sets balance to underflowed huge number.
After depositing 1 ether and calling Collect(2 ether) when MinSum is 1 ether and unlockTime passed, the reference reverts while the buggy sends 2 ether and underflows balance to 2^256-1.

After depositing 1.5 ether and calling Collect(1.5 ether) when MinSum is 1 ether and unlockTime has passed, the reference contract successfully sends 1.5 ether and reduces balance to 0, while the buggy contract (missing balance >= _am check) also succeeds but underflows balance to 2^256-1, causing c.Acc(user).balance to differ.

After user deposits 0.5 ether and calls Collect(0.5 ether) when MinSum is 0.4 ether and unlockTime has passed, the reference reduces balance to 0, while the buggy contract (missing balance >= _am check) also succeeds but underflows balance to 2^256-1.
